To determine the minimum number of squares that must be cut from a 7×7 chessboard so that the remaining squares cannot form a domino, we need to consider the properties of a domino and the structure of the chessboard. A domino covers exactly two adjacent squares, either horizontally or vertically. Therefore, to prevent the remaining squares from forming a domino, we need to ensure that no two adjacent squares remain.

A 7×7 chessboard has 49 squares. If we cut out squares in such a way that no two remaining squares are adjacent, we can achieve this by cutting out squares in a checkerboard pattern. In a checkerboard pattern, every square is surrounded by squares of the opposite color, and no two squares of the same color are adjacent. This means that if we cut out all the squares of one color, the remaining squares will be of the other color, and no two of them will be adjacent.

In a 7×7 chessboard, there are 25 squares of one color and 24 squares of the other color. Therefore, cutting out all 25 squares of one color will leave 24 squares of the other color, and these 24 squares will not be able to form a domino because no two of them are adjacent.

Thus, the minimum number of squares that must be cut from a 7×7 chessboard so that the remaining squares cannot form a domino is 25.
